item.title: From Kindness to Leadership: Calvert's Lighthouse Honorees
item.description: Calvert County Public Schools names first Superintendent's Lighthouse Award honorees including Harmony Downs, Brooke Boteler, Channing Swanson, Renee Reid, Cheryl Dick and Willanette Thomas-Lohr for embodying district values through leadership, kindness and service.

item.title: 50-Pound Bundle of Joy: Maru Seeks Forever Home in Charles County
item.description: Meet Maru, a lively 1.5-year-old, 50-pound dog at Charles County Animal Care Center in Hughesville. This enthusiastic cheerleader offers constant encouragement, walks and snuggles. Available for adoption Monday-Friday 11am-4pm and Saturday 10am-3pm.

item.title: Special Consensus Brings 50th Anniversary Tour to Calvert Elks
item.description: Special Consensus, marking 50 years with two Grammy nominations, makes its Southern Maryland debut on April 19, 2026, at the Calvert Elks Lodge in Prince Frederick. Doors open noon, show at 2 p.m. Tickets $23. The sixth concert in the popular bluegrass series.

item.title: Carnival Vibes Hit La Plata as CSM Marks 40 Years of Youth Programs
item.description: The College of Southern Maryland hosts a free 40th Anniversary Bash for Kids and Teen College on Saturday, March 28, 2026, from 12-4 p.m. at La Plata Campus Parking Lot 3. Enjoy games, treats, program info and community summer camp details for ages 5-17. Rain location in ST Building Atrium.

item.title: Annapolis Paintball Incident Leads to Assault Charges Against Teen
item.description: Anne Arundel County Police arrested a 14-year-old on March 21, 2026, in Annapolis after he allegedly shot an adult male in the face with a paintball gun in the 600 block of Admiral Drive. The teen faces first-degree assault and reckless endangerment charges.

item.title: New Algebra Pathway for CCPS Students
item.description: Charles County Public Schools will roll out Maryland's new math policy in 2026-2027 featuring an integrated Algebra I and II pathway, daily instruction for kindergarten through grade 8, and structured support for students needing help. Two public information sessions are planned for April 30 at Westlake High School in Waldorf and May 11 on Zoom. Registration is requested.

item.title: Thousands turn out — again — as third ‘No Kings’ rallies take over Maryland streets
item.description: They were political heavy-hitters and grandmothers, candidates and musicians, activists and several hundred regular Joes. They were angry about a litany of Trump administration policies, but particularly focused on recent immigration raids. There was chanting and costumes and signs. Lots of signs. item.title: Morrison’s No-Hitter Lifts CNU Past St. Mary’s
item.description: St. Mary’s College of Maryland baseball fell 13-0 to No. 16 Christopher Newport University with Ryan Morrison tossing a complete-game no-hitter and eight strikeouts. The Seahawks were held hitless while the Captains erupted for seven runs in the fifth. SMCM returns to United East Conference play at home Wednesday April 1 versus Penn State Harrisburg.

item.title: Waldorf Man Killed in Temple Hills Crash
item.description: Prince George’s County Police are investigating the March 27, 2026, fatal collision on Branch Avenue in Temple Hills that killed 28-year-old Christopher Umanzor of Waldorf. His vehicle struck another car from behind, veered off the road and hit a guardrail. The other driver and passenger were uninjured. Tips sought for case 26-0016050.

item.description: After two years of struggling to get over the finish line, advocates hope this is the year they pass legislation ensuring Marylanders have access to emergency abortions during severe, life-threatening medical complications. item.title: Balanced Attack Powers SMCM Past Wilson in UEC Debut
item.description: St. Mary's College of Maryland women's lacrosse team cruised to a 17-2 victory over Wilson College on March 28, 2026, in Chambersburg, Pa., to open United East Conference play. Three Seahawks posted four points each as the team snapped a four-game skid with dominant offense and defense.

item.title: Bipartisan Effort Targets Maryland Health Care Cost Drivers
item.description: The Bipartisan Policy Center's new Healthcare Affordability Initiative aims to address root causes of high health care costs in Maryland and nationally. With 55% of Marylanders reporting affordability burdens, the effort focuses on prescription drugs and bipartisan reforms to improve access without shifting costs.

item.title: Library Giving Day Starts Month of Support for Local Branches
item.description: Charles County Public Library kicks off Library Giving Month in April 2026 with a $20,000 goal to fund programs and services. Events include a book-themed tattoo fundraiser on April 10 and A Magical Evening on April 17. Donations support lifelong learning across Southern Maryland.

item.title: Maryland Implements New Striped Bass Seasons Starting April 1
item.description: Maryland’s new striped bass fishing regulations begin April 1, 2026, with catch-and-release in April, harvest May-July and September-December, and a full August closure to protect fish during high temperatures. The changes simplify rules and address six years of poor juvenile survival in the Chesapeake Bay.
